purpose: Cabazitaxel is used to treat prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and is no longer responding to hormone therapy. It is typically given when other chemotherapy treatments, like docetaxel, have already been tried. It helps slow the growth and spread of cancer cells.
how_it_works: Cabazitaxel works by interfering with the way cancer cells divide and multiply. It basically jams the machinery that cancer cells need to split into new cells, causing them to stop growing and eventually die. Because it targets rapidly dividing cells, it can slow down or shrink tumors.
common_side_effects: Feeling very tired or weak, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite, hair loss, numbness or tingling in hands and feet, low blood cell counts (which can increase your risk of infection, bruising, or bleeding), back pain, and fever.
warnings: This medication can seriously lower your white blood cell count, making it much easier to catch dangerous infections — call your doctor right away if you have a fever of 100.4°F or higher. It can also cause severe allergic reactions during the infusion, so you will be given pre-medications beforehand. Kidney and liver problems can occur. It is not safe during pregnancy and can harm an unborn baby. Always tell your care team about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with cabazitaxel.
typical_dosing: Cabazitaxel is given by IV infusion (into a vein) in a clinic or hospital, usually once every 3 weeks. Each infusion takes about 1 hour. Your doctor will determine the exact dose based on your body size and overall health. You will also be given steroid and antihistamine medications before each infusion to help prevent reactions.
